exposure: type of fetal anomaly (anencephaly, meningomyelocele/spina bifida, cyanotic congenital heart disease, congenital diaphragmatic hernia, omphalocele, gastroschisis, cleft lip and/or palate, hypospadias, limb anomaly, chromosomal disorders, multiple anomalies)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 35,760,626 pregnancies at 20 weeks or greater, with 105,002 involving isolated or multiple fetal anomalies and the rest having no fetal anomaly.
finding: The presence of most fetal anomalies, with the exception of gastroschisis and limb anomaly, was associated with an increased risk of severe maternal morbidity (SMM), with the risk varying by anomaly type.
